issues.title: Scattermapbox maki symbols plot on map, but not legend
issues.body:
Hi Plotly, 

First, thank you for all the fantastic work you do. 

I am a big fan of / heavy user of the plotly.go objects that render maps (Scattermapbox / Choroplethmapbox).

I have noticed, however, that when setting the symbol type to a maki symbol, it will render it on the map - but not the legend. This feels like a bug, as there is also a colour associated with the legend item that is not matched anywhere on the plot / by the symbol (except in hovertext). 

Reproducible example below: 

```python
import os
import plotly.graph_objects as go

mapboxt = os.getenv('MAPBOX_TOKEN') # a mapbox token

lats = [52.370216, 53.2191696,  50.851368, 51.8125626]
lons = [4.895168,  6.5666699, 5.690973, 5.8372264 ]

fig = go.Figure()

scatt = go.Scattermapbox(
            lat=lats,
            lon=lons,
            mode='markers',
            hovertext=['Amsterdam', 'Groningen',  'Maastricht', 'Nijmegen'],  
            hoverinfo='text',                 
            below='',                 
            marker=dict(symbol ='hospital'),
            name ='my_fake_hospitals',
            showlegend=True)

fig.add_trace(scatt)

fig.update_layout(go.Layout(title_text ='Is it a hospital? No, it is a blue dot!', 
                            title_x=0.5, 
                            width=750, 
                            height=700,
                            mapbox = dict(center= dict(lat=52.370216, lon=4.895168),            
                                         accesstoken= mapboxt,
                                         zoom=5,
                                         style="light"
                                       )))

fig
```

Finally, as a side note, some maki symbols plot whilst others do not. I have determined through trial and error that this is down to whether or not the MapBox style includes these specific symbol types. Using custom Mapbox styles, therefore, may silently break the maki functionality as well. 

Thanks you for your attention.

issues.title: Scattergl and px.line fill and continuous error bands don't appear
issues.body:
## Summary

Using the `fill` and `fillcolor` parameters on `scattergl` traces (to produce continuous error bands, [for example](https://plotly.com/python/continuous-error-bars/)) does not work.


## Issue

The issue is specific to `scattergl` traces: the same parameters work fine with `scatter` traces.  To avoid the problem with `plotly.express` `px.line()` calls requires using `render_mode="svg"` to avoid the use of `scattergl` traces.

Using `graph_objects` has the some problem: one must use `go.Scatter()` and not `go.Scattergl()` to get error bands.

The reference for `scattergl` traces (https://plotly.com/python/reference/scattergl/#scattergl-fill) indicates that the behaviour should be the same as for `scatter`.

## Specs

**Python Version**: `3.8.6`
**Plotly Version**: `4.14.3`
**Kaleido Version**: `0.2.1`

* For image exports to be pasted here (they all looked the same as rendered in the browser) 

**Browsers**: Firefox 88.0, Safari 12.1.1

## Example

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# dummy data
x = np.linspace(0, 10000, num=10_000)

df = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': x**2})
df['y_err_plus'] = df['y'] * 1.1
df['y_err_minus'] = df['y'] * 0.95
```

```python
# use webgl and no fill

fig = (
px
 .line(
    df, x='x', y=['y', 'y_err_minus','y_err_plus'], 
    render_mode='webgl')
 .update_traces(
     fill='tonexty', fillcolor='red',
     selector={'name':'y_err_plus'}
 )
)
fig
```

![fill_test](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13930443/118091671-71fed500-b40e-11eb-944f-b0e896bb0c9d.png)


```python
# use svg to get fill

fig = (
px
 .line(
    df, x='x', y=['y', 'y_err_minus','y_err_plus'], 
    render_mode='svg')
 .update_traces(
     fill='tonexty', fillcolor='red',
     selector={'name':'y_err_plus'}
 )
)
fig
```

![fill_working](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13930443/118091719-7dea9700-b40e-11eb-855a-b09b2bc5aa72.png)


## Sanity Check: fill to zero works?

Yes.

```python
fig = (
px
.line(
    df, x='x', y='y', 
    render_mode='webgl')
.update_traces(fill='tozeroy')
)

fig
```

![fill_zero](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13930443/118092085-f94c4880-b40e-11eb-84ad-376fef4bd621.png)

issues.title: Add Support for Velocity Arrows in Scatter 3D Graphs
issues.body:
**Original issue description:**

I propose adding a feature to the scatter and scatter3d graph types in Plotly to support velocity arrows. This feature would allow users to display directional arrows, enhancing data visualization for applications that involve vector fields, velocities, forces, or any data represented by direction and magnitude.

**Update 31 Aug 2026:**

- 2D quiver now supported with `go.Quiver()` (as of v7.0.0)
- Our answer for 3D quiver is `go.Cone()`, but it has limitations:

> For 3D though, Cone() isn't really an arrow. To get a velocity vector you **have to combine a Cone (head) with a Scatter3d line (shaft) and keep them in sync manually**. **The bigger issue is that cone size is in data units while line width is in pixels — so on zoom the head and shaft drift out of proportion** (head swallows the shaft, or disappears entirely).
> 
> What I was after is the **3D analogue of Quiver**: takes x, y, z, u, v, w, draws shaft + attached head, with the head sized in pixels so it stays legible under zoom and rotation.

comments.body: thanks @AlmogHadad - if you would like to work on a pull request, we would be happy to review it.

comments.body:
Thanks @emilykl — go.Quiver() for 2D is great news.

For 3D though, Cone() isn't really an arrow. To get a velocity vector you **have to combine a Cone (head) with a Scatter3d line (shaft) and keep them in sync manually**. **The bigger issue is that cone size is in data units while line width is in pixels — so on zoom the head and shaft drift out of proportion** (head swallows the shaft, or disappears entirely).

What I was after is the **3D analogue of Quiver**: takes x, y, z, u, v, w, draws shaft + attached head, with the head sized in pixels so it stays legible under zoom and rotation.

comments.body:
Hi @NoniosTheMad @gvwilson, I investigated the root cause of this behavior in plotly.py.

### Root Cause
In Figure.add_hline() and dd_vline(), xclude_empty_subplots defaults to True.

When a figure is initialized via make_subplots(), _has_subplots() is True. During _add_annotation_like() in [plotly/basedatatypes.py](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py/blob/main/plotly/basedatatypes.py#L1611):
`python
if exclude_empty_subplots and (
    not self._subplot_not_empty(
        xref, yref, selector=bool(exclude_empty_subplots)
    )
):
    return self
`
Since self.data is empty at that point, _subplot_not_empty() evaluates to False for all subplots. The shape is silently dropped (
eturn self) instead of being appended to layout.shapes. When  ig.add_trace(...) is called afterwards, the shape is already lost.

In contrast, on a bare go.Figure(), _has_subplots() is False, which resets 
ow and col to None. This bypasses the subplot grid check entirely and allows dd_hline() to succeed before data is added.

### Proposed Fix
We can adjust the check in _add_annotation_like() so that xclude_empty_subplots only filters subplots when the figure actually contains plotted data (i.e.  ool(self.data)), preserving reference lines configured prior to populating traces.

Happy to open a PR with regression unit tests covering dd_hline/dd_vline on unpopulated subplots if this direction sounds good to the maintainers!
comments.author: ioseba

comments.body:
I think a better idea would be to skip `exclude_empty_subplots` when it's obvious that the user wants the line such as:
- Only one subplot exists
- The user passes in a specific subplot via `row`/`col`

comments.body:
Thanks for sharing your perspective @camdecoster! That is a really interesting point — when specific 
ow and col arguments are passed, the intent to target that exact cell is very clear.

At the same time, we completely understand the maintainers' rationale discussed earlier in #5254 regarding how xclude_empty_subplots was designed to avoid cluttering empty grids. The tricky part from a user standpoint is just the subtle order-of-operations effect: calling dd_hline() before versus after dd_trace() behaves differently because the shape gets dropped if traces aren't present yet.

@emilykl @gvwilson Whenever you have a chance to take a look, we would love to hear your thoughts on what you feel is the best direction for plotly.py:
1. Keeping the current behavior as-is and recommending xclude_empty_subplots=False (perhaps adding a small note in the docstring to help users who run into this).
2. Or allowing a small tweak so that explicit 
ow/col targets aren't dropped before data is populated.
